record.paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
record.original_question: For the normalized delayed Pielou harvesting equation x_{n+1} = b x_n/(1 + x_{n-1}) - h with b > 1 and h > 1, characterize the largest persistent set D_h of initial conditions. In particular, determine whether D_h is closed and whether D_h is connected.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order scalar difference equation
  x_{n+1} = b x_n / (1 + x_{n-1}) − h,  n = 0, 1, 2, …,
with parameters b > 1 and h > 1, and with initial conditions (x_{-1}, x_0) ∈ [0, ∞)^2. Define the persistent set
  D_h = { (x_{-1}, x_0) ∈ [0, ∞)^2 : the resulting solution (x_n)_{n ≥ -1} satisfies x_n ≥ 0 for all n ≥ -1 and liminf_{n → ∞} x_n > 0 },
i.e., the largest set of nonnegative initial conditions whose forward orbit stays nonnegative and is bounded away from 0.

Provide an explicit characterization of D_h. In particular, determine:
(i) whether D_h is a closed subset of [0, ∞)^2;
(ii) whether D_h is connected.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches indicate that, while the persistent set for the Pielou harvesting equation has been described explicitly in certain regimes (notably for h < 1 via a connection with a Lyness-type equation), the characterization of the largest persistent set D_h in the harvesting-dominant regime b > 1, h > 1, and in particular whether D_h is closed and connected, does not appear to have been settled in the literature. No subsequent paper resolving this specific open problem was located.

status_evidence.title: The dynamics of some discrete models with delay under the effect of constant yield harvesting
status_evidence.snippet: Pielou's equation was considered... a connection with a Lyness type equation has been established at certain harvesting level, which is used to give an explicit description of a persistent set... when h < 1.
status_evidence.claim: Persistent-set descriptions exist for the low-harvesting regime h < 1, but the case h > 1 is treated as an open problem.
